beats.care: These roads would reshape your daily commute for years. Residents want that money spent on metro links and more buses.
beats.what: On Sunday, residents linked hands on Indiranagar's 80 Feet and 100 Feet Roads and at Rose Garden junction near Jayanagar.
beats.why: B-SMILE has proposed 13 elevated corridors. Residents fear dust, lost trees and parks, and damage to Cauvery water pipelines.

cards.body: The plan covers about 126 km, according to Asianet Newsable. Bengaluru Central MP P.C. Mohan has asked for independent traffic and environment studies.
cards.caption: Estimated cost of all 13 corridors

cards.body: In the south, residents oppose a 17-km corridor from Ragigudda to Kanakapura Road near NICE Road. One organiser asked why a road is needed parallel to the existing Green Line metro.
Protesters say they are not anti-development. One organiser said: "We are telling the government to strengthen public transport."

cards.q: What would fix your commute faster?

opts: Spend on public transport instead of flyovers
cards.q: What is the residents' main demand?
cards.why: Residents want metro upgrades, buses and last-mile links prioritised over more elevated roads.

hook: Why are Bengaluru residents saying *no to new flyovers*?

learn.t: The Ragigudda–Thalaghattapura corridor's own project report projects Rose Garden junction peak traffic nearly doubling by 2035.

tldr: Hundreds of residents formed human chains in Indiranagar and near Rose Garden on Sunday against proposed elevated corridors.
watch: South Bengaluru residents plan to send a formal objection to B-SMILE within two weeks.
